old_value: {"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-itzv","title":"Prevent delayed prior fragments from contaminating replacement SCHC sessions","description":"Security review of spec/03-adaptation.md §5.6 and draft-lichen-schc-lora-00 terminal hold-down found that the 60-second tombstone does not fully disambiguate packets when T=0. During hold-down, regular late fragments are discarded without a normative tombstone high-water update; after expiry, any Regular/All-1 with counter greater than the stored high-water may create a session. Once a replacement session is active, there is also no rule requiring every admitted fragment to be newer than an immutable session-admission floor. Because the link replay window accepts unseen out-of-order counters, a delayed authenticated fragment from the prior packet can create or contaminate a replacement context, especially when duplicate retransmissions were allocated after the frame that produced terminal success. Define a safe session-opening/admission barrier (or a bounded lifetime/DTag mechanism) that cannot admit prior-packet fragments, advance the relevant terminal barrier on every authenticated late message, and add state-machine vectors for delayed unique regular/All-1 frames both during hold-down and after a replacement starts.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"me@mark.atwood.name","created_at":"2026-08-24T13:27:40.146236Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-08-24T13:27:40.146236Z"}
